proposedchanges.title: Trump Taj Mahal Violated Anti-Money-Laundering Reporting Requirements at Least 106 Times
proposedchanges.description_medium: The Trump Taj Mahal opened in Atlantic City in April 1990. During its first year and a half, the casino failed to file required reports on large cash transactions at least 106 times, according to the supplied account. Casinos had to report one-day cash-outs over $10,000, including identifying details. The reported violations concern compliance; they do not establish that the casino knowingly laundered money.
proposedchanges.description_long:
The Trump Taj Mahal opened in Atlantic City in April 1990. During its first year and a half, the casino failed to meet federal anti-money-laundering reporting requirements at least 106 times, according to the timeline. Casinos were required to report when a patron cashed out more than $10,000 in one day and provide information such as the person’s name and address. These reports helped regulators review large gambling transactions.

The failures involved required disclosures, not a finding that the casino itself laundered money or that every transaction was criminal. The supplied account does not identify the individual cash-outs, explain the casino’s response, or specify the enforcement outcome at the time. That limits what can be concluded about the intent behind each missed filing. The report documents repeated noncompliance at Trump’s Atlantic City casino while leaving the transactions and consequences unexamined. Failure to submit required reports can weaken oversight, but the record does not show the source of the funds or prove criminal intent.

evidencebasis: The synopsis and long identify at least 106 reporting failures, the $10,000 threshold, and required identifying details. They do not establish money laundering, transaction sources, intent, or enforcement outcome. Both URLs remain unchanged.
